topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture on cancer evolution and outlines the session's core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how acquired mutations and epigenetic modifications drive clonal succession and selective growth advantages in pre-malignant tissues.

topics.label: Cell of origin and the cancer stem cell model
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate how tissue hierarchies and stemness properties influence tumor initiation and propagation across different cancer types.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how inflammatory stimuli and stromal interactions provide essential permissive signals for tumor transformation and growth.

topics.label: Experimental technologies for studying tumor architecture and evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It reviews genomic and spatial profiling methods used to track mutational timing and cell-to-cell interactions within tumors.

topics.label: Synthesis of multi-factorial cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It integrates genetic, epigenetic, cell-of-origin, and microenvironmental factors into a unified model of Darwinian cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture and provides a brief preview of the upcoming session.
